Title: AKU- IED, EA Retreat
NewsSummary: Reflection and Strategic Planning for Faculty and Support Staff
NewsContent:
The Aga Khan University-Institute for Educational Development, East Africa (AKU-IED, EA) kicked off the year with a three-day retreat from January 24th to January 26th, 2024, held in Zanzibar, Tanzania. The purpose of the retreat was to reflect on the achievements of 2023, celebrate milestones, tackle challenges, and establish priorities for the year 2024. The event was attended by a group of over 24 staff and faculty members. Prof. Jane Rarieya, the Dean of AKU-IED, EA, and Prof. Tashmin Khamis, the Vice Provost of AKU-Quality, Teaching & Learning, were facilitators of the retreat.

"Our objective of having this retreat at the beginning of the year is to familiarize with the strategic plan activities for 2024, reflect on past year and implications for 2024 and identify key challenges and mitigation strategies. Additionally, plan for institutional and individual activities and targets aligned to IED, EA's strategic plan activities 2024 and beyond. This retreat was coupled with some team building and fun activities", emphasized Prof. Jane Rarieya, Dean, AKU- IED, EA.

At the retreat, faculty and support staff achieved clarity as they aligned themselves with the 2024 strategic direction of AKU-IED, EA. They sharpened a range of skills aimed at strengthening capacities across various units, including programs, research, the Centre for Continuing Education and Lifelong Learning (CELL), and projects. The overarching objective was to cultivate synergies in implementing the 2024 strategic plan for IED, EA. Each participant seized the opportunity to articulate their role as a pillar of excellence within the university. The dedication to this commitment was clearly reflected in the testimonials provided by the new faculty at AKU-IED, EA:

"The retreat has been fruitful to me as it has introduced and actively engaged me as I internalize the IED, EA 2024 strategic plan. It has enhanced my bonding to other units of the AKU family and made me understand how we can work together as a team to bring synergy and impactful outcome, said, Esther Kibga'', Faculty at IED, EA.

"The retreat provided opportunities for gainful interactions with colleagues and the leadership of IED, EA. It has offered insights into dialogic engagements, brainstorming, reviewing and generally reflecting as individuals and as a group. This was quite fulfilling because an environment for sharing ideas was cultivated.  Consequently, I got an opportunity to generate, identify and vividly see my role in the overall organogram at IED, EA", emphasized Howard Omukami, Faculty at IED, EA.

AKU-IED, EA remains committed to embodying strategic thinking, ethical practices, and excellence in pursuit of its mission to advocate for quality education across East Africa and beyond.
